LESSON: PRESSURE

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Force and Energy
Topic 3.2: Pressure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Pressure. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the applications of pressure in solids and liquids?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids
2. identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids
3. appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PRESSURE
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Pressure helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: PRESSURE
Study Pressure like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Pressure” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids

What this means
In this part you learn to identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Pressure matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Pressure this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Pressure is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Pressure” around your school. (skill: demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids)

Example 2: Say why Pressure matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Pressure this week. (skill: appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Pressure to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids.
3. Practise this skill: identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the applications of pressure in solids and liquids.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Pressure from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Pressure: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Pressure?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the applications of pressure in solids and liquids?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Pressure means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate pressure in solids and liquids.
5. Be able to: identify applications of pressure in solids and liquids.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
